claim_summaries.claim: Finite two-broadcast error epsilon on m supplied states implies one EB reconstruction with worst trace error at most L epsilon + sqrt(m ln(m)/(2*2^L)); a-net extension yields e_n <= 2a + L b_n + sqrt(N_n(a) ln N_n(a)/(2*2^L)).

The quantum-locking ensemble has average state distance 1/2 and accessible information exponentially small in q despite 2*3^q labels, refuting a universal one-stage lower bound of order average_distance^2/ln(m). This blocks the natural local proof for replacing m by ln(m), but does not refute every stronger global finite-cover theorem.

overall_status: SUBSTANTIVE_INITIAL_FROZEN; global sharper finite-cover theorem remains open
next_gate: Cross-exposed audit of stronger cover estimates, with optimal broadcaster error explicitly bounded.
